state_of_play.narrative: The long end blinked, and everything that had been selling turned. The US Treasury said on 19 August that it will at least double its liquidity-support buyback operations for longer-dated coupons - from a $2bn cap to at least $4bn an operation, across the 10-20 and 20-30 year sectors, running from 9 September into early November. It is a plumbing measure, not new spending, but it arrived two days after the 30-year hit 5.31%, its highest since 2007, and the tape treated it as the authorities noticing. The 10-year fell 5bp to 4.65% after testing near 4.75%; the S&P 500 rose 0.21% to 7,707.98; the VIX fell 6% to 14.89; and bitcoin rose 7.27% to $69,381, above $69,000 for the first time since June, with about $1.44bn of shorts liquidated. Gold rose 1.10% to $4,539, EUR/USD 0.86% to 1.168, and Asia bounced - Nikkei +1.38%, MSCI EM +1.18%. Underneath it, two company facts did more for the book's theses than the macro did. SK hynix's board approved a KRW 40tn (~$28.6bn) repurchase and full cancellation of its own shares - the largest treasury cancellation ever by a listed Korean company, about 3.3% of shares outstanding, buying from 20 August - and raised its shareholder-return target to over half of 2025-27 free cash flow. A company answering a 9% one-day fall with a record cancellation and two new fabs is not behaving like a cycle top; memory rebounded, SK hynix +6%, SanDisk +5%, Micron +3%. And Nebius launched a $4.5bn convertible bond offering, $2.75bn due 2030 and $1.75bn due 2034, falling as much as 13.7% on it - the neocloud financing leg tested in the primary market, in public, four days after the long end peaked. Three things this page said yesterday were wrong and are corrected here. The 50% Section 338 duties on Canada did not take effect - Trump paused them for three days, to 22 August, less than two hours before the deadline, on a deal Carney says still needs work. The Nasdaq-100 inclusion of CoreWeave, Nebius and Astera Labs is a June event, effective 22 June, not this month's flows evidence. And Fincantieri's $30m landing-ship award is dated 15 April, four months old and predating the shipbuilding memorandum it was credited to. Larger than all three: this book had never recorded that the Supreme Court struck down the IEEPA tariffs 6-3 on 20 February, terminating them on 24 February and taking the weighted average applied US tariff rate from 14.9% to 8.2%. Target's Q2 the same day booked $994m of tariff refunds and doubled its profit on them. The reshoring-by-tariff driver is cut from 5 to 3. Brent $91.91, gold $4,539, VIX 14.89.

Bloomberg reported on 10 August that Rocket Lab is cautioning on fresh risks that could push Neutron's debut into 2027, and that the 2026 window is narrowing, with Stage 1 tank production aligned to a Q4 2026 pad delivery. investible_themes.read: Raised from conviction 2 to 3 on a price leg and a political leg moving together, having been cut to 2 a day earlier on falling odds alone. Bitcoin rose 7.27% to $69,381, above $69,000 for the first time since June, with roughly $1.44bn of short positions liquidated; ether jumped alongside it. The drivers named in coverage are not crypto-native, which is the interesting part: the Treasury's decision to at least double long-dated bond buybacks, the resulting bond rally and softer dollar, an SEC crypto proposal, and Trump publicly calling on Congress to advance market-structure legislation. That last one bears directly on the leg that was cut: the CLARITY Act's Senate procedural vote is still set for 15 September with cloture filed, and the ~25% Polymarket odds recorded a day ago were priced before the president's push. The odds are not re-pinned in this sweep and are not claimed to have moved - the upgrade rests on the price leg and the political leg, with the legislative odds carried as unre-verified.

2025 revenue $30.9m (from $23m) with a $192.6m net loss; Honeywell and Cambridge Quantum retain ~82%
The quantum radar entry's expression line had listed only IONQ, RGTI, QBTS and IBM
signals.assessment: A coverage gap of this desk's own, closed. It widens the basket but does not confirm flows - a flat debut is not a demand signal, so the score stays 4 of 5.

signals.headline: Home Depot beats and reaffirms guidance in 'frozen housing market conditions'
summary: Beat on both revenue and EPS on 18 August and reaffirmed full-year guidance
CFO Richard McPhail described the customer as 'a healthy cohort' who has not returned to big projects
Reported under an interim office of the chief executive after Ted Decker's medical leave, announced 12 August
signals.assessment: Weak housing, not a weak consumer. It cuts against the labour-turn entry rather than for it. Target reports 19 Aug, Walmart 20 Aug.

signals.headline: China's loan prime rates unchanged for a 14th month; still no answer to the July miss
summary: One-year LPR 3.00% and five-year 3.50%, unchanged at record lows; the August fixing is due 20 August
The RRR and the policy rate both remain available and unspent after a 50bp RRR cut in May
A search result describing a large August 2026 PBoC stimulus package was checked and rejected - it is the September 2024 package resurfacing
signals.assessment: An observed absence of policy, which for a policy-driven economy is itself the signal. Second consecutive cycle.

signals.headline: Prediction markets take two regulatory hits: Kalshi restrained in Washington, Polymarket debanked
summary: A judge ordered Kalshi to stop offering most wagers in Washington state on 12 August
JPMorgan debanked Polymarket on regulatory concerns on 13 August
Kalshi spent $500,000 lobbying federal policymakers in Q2 2026, more than in any prior quarter
signals.assessment: The regulatory risk this desk logged as a caveat on 18 Aug has converted into a court order and a banking-access problem. The leg is weaker, not stronger.

signals.headline: Q2 13Fs: SpaceX and Alphabet bought, NVIDIA and Broadcom sold
summary: All nine institutions disclosing a SpaceX position added to or increased it; Alphabet drew 11 buyers including Berkshire
NVIDIA and Broadcom saw net selling; CoreWeave and Seagate gained momentum
Situational Awareness LP filed on 14 August and is characterised as peak AI concentration ahead of an unwind - its reported AUM and return figures come from a secondary aggregator and are NOT adopted
signals.assessment: Divided, and rotating rather than adding. The 17 Aug put-book trace re-enters here as new evidence after being formally retired on 18 Aug.

signals.headline: US-Iran 60-day deadline expires with no deal and no extension
summary: The 60-day window set in a June memorandum lapsed on 17 August, deadlocked on Hormuz and on frozen Iranian funds
Neither side would extend it, and Iran does not consider the clock to have started
Washington has now turned on Oman, the channel through which the Hormuz-management talks were running
signals.assessment: The negotiated route has lapsed rather than stalled. This is the energy-premium theme's driver hardening, not easing.

signals.headline: US 30-year Treasury yield reaches 5.31%, the highest since 2007
summary: Heavy issuance plus tariff and energy inflation drove the long bond to a 19-year high on 17 August
The UK 30-year gilt sat near 5.77% the same day, with the 10-year back above 5%
Yesterday this desk called the gilt move a UK-specific transmission - both G7 long ends moved together
signals.assessment: CORRECTION to yesterday's read. The oil premium is in the US curve too, which raises the discount rate under every AI-capex model.

signals.headline: China's July activity misses across the board; still no policy answer
summary: Industrial output +4.5% y/y vs 4.8% expected; retail sales +0.6% vs 1.5% expected
Fixed-asset investment -6.7% year-to-date; urban unemployment up to 5.2%
As of 18 August the PBoC has not responded - policy shifted to a data-dependent hold in 1H26 after a 50bp RRR cut in May
signals.assessment: The easing ammunition exists and is unspent. Absence of a response is itself the finding this run.

signals.headline: TrendForce sees conventional DRAM contract prices +13-18% q/q, NAND +10-15%
summary: Published 13 August; HBM4 costs $31-32/GB against HBM3E at $17-18/GB
Samsung's entire 2026 HBM capacity is sold out; HBM4 yields reported near 80%
SK hynix holds 50-55% of the HBM market
signals.assessment: Third independent supply-side confirmation in a fortnight. The shortage-not-cycle framing keeps getting better evidenced.

signals.headline: Fluence starts construction on a 400 MWh German grid battery and signs two hyperscaler MSAs
summary: Fluence and LEAG began building the Heinersbrueck GridBattery on 14 August - their second joint project
Master supply agreements signed with two major hyperscale datacentres; datacentre pipeline +30% since Q1 at ~12 GWh contracted
Base Power raised $1bn on 3 August for a US-manufactured battery platform
signals.assessment: Storage is the AI-power leg that delivers inside this cycle, and it is now shipping in Europe as well as the US.

signals.headline: US opens Navy shipbuilding to foreign yards; Hanwha Ocean +5.6%, Fincantieri also higher
summary: National-security memorandum signed 14 August (this desk previously dated it 15 August)
Covers surface combatants, consolidated cargo replenishment tankers and roll-on/roll-off vessels
Every vessel after the first two must be built in the US, with possible technology transfer attached
signals.assessment: A second listed price response widens the basket beyond Korea. Still 4 of 5 - flows are the missing criterion.

signals.headline: CORRECTED: the CLARITY Act has a Senate floor vote scheduled for 15 September
summary: Cloture was filed on the motion to proceed before the recess, keeping the bill on the docket
Banking Committee advanced it 15-9 on 14 May; a revised draft was published 1 June
Open disputes: government ethics, illicit finance, and stablecoin yield and rewards
signals.assessment: Yesterday this desk wrote that passage was likely slipping to 2027. That was over-read - the delay is real but dated.

signals.headline: CORRECTED: the 401(k) private-assets executive order dates to August 2025, not this month
summary: The executive order was signed 7 August 2025; Blackstone stood up its DC unit in October 2025
The 2026-dated catalyst is the DOL proposal of 30 March 2026, on which the listed alt managers rose
The radar entry's price leg therefore belongs to March, not to August
signals.assessment: An entry promoted yesterday on a year-old catalyst. Held at 4 of 5 and re-dated rather than quietly fixed.

signals.headline: MSTR pinned from a quoted close at $93.95 after four failed attempts
summary: Traded $93.82-$94.48 on 17 August, closing $93.95; market cap $35.76bn
Against the $91.39 call of 14 July the exit flag is +2.8% - leaning wrong
The evening pass had derived ~$93.0 by inverting an analyst target percentage; the derivation was close
signals.assessment: The 'wire a price feed or close the flag' dilemma is resolved: a direct price search works. The flag stays open.

signals.headline: CoreWeave Q2: revenue $2.58bn (+112%), backlog $104bn (+246%)
summary: Adjusted loss $1.03/sh vs $1.22 expected; shares rose ~13-14% after hours and ~19% across the post-print stretch
FY26 guidance raised to $12.4-13.2bn with capex of $35-39bn
51 active datacentres, 1.5 GW active power, ~3.7 GW contracted
signals.assessment: The master factor's biggest test, and the payer passed. With the 30Y at 5.31% the financing leg is now the open question.

signals.headline: Nebius Q2: revenue $582m (+454%), adjusted EBITDA positive $236m
summary: EPS -$0.12 against -$0.82 expected; full-year guidance reaffirmed at $3.0-3.4bn
Four core contracts averaging over $1bn each; customer prepayments cover 50-60% of associated capex
Secondary coverage cites $575m and +514% - the company release is the anchor, the divergence is logged not adopted
signals.assessment: Pre-paid, contracted capacity funded by customers rather than by debt alone. Shares rose ~34% post-print.

signals.headline: Lumentum revenue $1.01bn (+109%) on record 800G, with 1.6T ramping
summary: EPS $3.23 vs $2.97; non-GAAP gross margin crossed 50%
Record 800G cloud transceiver shipments; 1.6T production started on plan
Stock +14.19% on 12 August
signals.assessment: The print that promoted optics to confirmed. No fresh evidence this run - the promotion is one week old and holding.

signals.headline: Rheinmetall Q2 sales +69.8%, backlog EUR 80.4bn, but H1 cash flow -EUR 1.6bn
summary: Operating profit +115%; shares fell 5.7% post-print on the cash outflow, then +5.5% on 16 August
Backlog EUR 80.4bn with ~70% firm orders, up from the EUR 64bn this desk had carried
The kill-watch receded this run: the 2026 truces were short and failed, and the EU agreed a EUR 90bn Ukraine loan on 23 April
signals.assessment: Strong orders sold on cash quality. The political driver improved; the cash-conversion question did not.

signals.headline: MP Materials' processed rare-earth revenue nearly quadruples to $94.4m
summary: Achieved after halting shipments of material to China for processing
Texas magnet operations added $16.5m revenue and $7.5m adjusted profit
Structural leg: the G7 agreed on 17 June to cap single-source rare-earth imports below 60% by 2030
signals.assessment: Conversion, not just a price pop. But August itself produced no fresh print - the domain is quiet on a strong base.
